questions.q: What two parts together identify a MySQL account?
options: Username and host pattern
Username and password only
Username and database name
Host pattern and database name
questions.explain: MySQL accounts are written 'username'@'host' — the same username at a different host is a genuinely separate account.

questions.q: Are 'app_svc'@'10.0.4.%' and 'app_svc'@'localhost' the same account or different accounts?
options: Different accounts, even though they share a username, because the host halves differ
The same account, since the username is identical
It depends on which one was created first
MySQL doesn't allow two accounts with the same username
questions.explain: MySQL treats each user@host pair as a distinct account with its own authentication and privileges.

questions.q: When multiple user@host patterns could match an incoming connection, which one does MySQL authenticate against?
options: The most specific matching host pattern
The first one created chronologically
The one with the shortest username
MySQL picks one at random
questions.explain: MySQL resolves ties by preferring the narrowest/most specific matching host pattern over a broader wildcard.

questions.q: What does ALTER USER 'analyst'@'192.168.1.%' ACCOUNT LOCK; do?
options: Disables the account's ability to authenticate without deleting it
Permanently deletes the account
Changes the account's host pattern to localhost
Grants the account additional privileges
questions.explain: ACCOUNT LOCK is a reversible way to disable login, useful for something like an employee on leave.

questions.q: If you run DROP USER 'analyst'@'192.168.1.%'; and an 'analyst'@'10.0.0.%' account also exists, what happens to the second account?
options: It is untouched — DROP USER removes only the exact user@host pair specified
It is also dropped, since the username matches
It is automatically locked
MySQL raises an error requiring both to be dropped together
questions.explain: DROP USER targets one specific user@host pair, not every account sharing that username.
